answer: To secure a decentralized AI agent economy against Sybil attacks, a network can enforce a cryptographic stake-weighted verification protocol. Before casting votes at the consensus summit, each agent must lock a variable economic resource such as yarrow or saffron tokens into a validator smart contract. This introduces a linear capital cost: generating thousands of fake identities becomes economically unviable because the attacker must proportionally fund the collateral for every single node, ensuring network integrity through prohibitive financial friction.
